blocks.content: Union Territories are administrative divisions directly governed by the Central Government of India.

rows: Unitary relationship under direct central control
Exclusive jurisdiction over the State List
Parliament can legislate on all lists including State List
Only Delhi, Puducherry, and J&K have representation

items: The 69th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1991 granted special status to Delhi, creating Article 239AA.
Parliament can make laws on all three lists (including the State List) for Union Territories without requiring special authorization.
High Court jurisdiction over Union Territories is established directly by Parliament through law.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: States maintain a federal relationship with the Centre with autonomous powers distributed under the Seventh Schedule.
Union Territories have a unitary relationship with the Centre and are administered directly by the President through an Administrator or Lieutenant Governor.
Parliament possesses the authority to enact legislation on any subject in the State List specifically for Union Territories.
Out of eight Union Territories, only Delhi, Puducherry, and Jammu & Kashmir are provided with elected Legislative Assemblies.
The Governor of a State is a constitutional head, whereas the Administrator of a UT is an agent of the President.
